subject: Auralis trial: acceptance criteria, timeline, and eval methodology
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Emma Carter <emma.carter@auralishealth.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Auralis trial: acceptance criteria, timeline, and eval methodology

Hi Emma / team — thanks again for the productive demo earlier. Quick recap and a proposed plan so we have aligned expectations before we hand off to ops/engineering.

Recap of agreed scope: Redwood will run a 3-week evaluative trial to validate model fit for Auralis' clinical note summarization use case. The goal is to determine whether Redwood can meet your accuracy and latency targets under a shadow/readonly run against a subset of real traffic.

Proposed acceptance criteria (please confirm or adjust):
- Quality: average rubric score >= 4.0/5 across three clinical note types (admit, discharge, progress).
- Safety/Hallucination: hallucination incidents <= 2% (high-confidence incorrect facts).
- Latency: P95 inference latency <= 300ms for payloads typical of your API (median expected ~150-200 tokens).
- Throughput: sustain your expected burst of ~20 TPS for 30s windows without error-rate increase >1%.

Evaluation approach (two parallel tracks):
1) Offline evals — Redwood evaluates a held-out set of 500 annotated notes you provide. We run our grading rubric and return per-example scores and error categories.
2) Shadow (online) — integrate a read-only shadow tap into a subset of production traffic for 5–7 business days (no traffic steering). We collect end-to-end latency, model confidence, and a sample of outputs for human review.

Draft timeline (flexible):
- Week 0 (this week): sign trial scope & NDAs; exchange data sample and security questionnaire.
- Week 1: onboarding + offline evals on supplied dataset.
- Week 2: shadow run (5 business days) + human grading of sampled outputs.
- Week 3: joint review, findings, and decision (go/no-go/next steps).

Owners: Redwood CS (Connors) — overall lead; Redwood Eval (Marissa) — offline rubric and scoring; Auralis PM (Emma) — business acceptance and example labeling.

Immediate asks from your side:
- Can you share a de-identified sample of 200–500 notes and your top 10 intents/edge cases to prioritize? (format: CSV or JSONL)
- Confirm whether security will need a live SOC2 evidence share or we can start with the standard questionnaire.
- Agree to the proposed acceptance criteria or suggest adjustments.

I've attached a one-page trial scope template for quick signoff. If that looks good, I'll schedule the kickoff and loop in engineering for the shadow instrumentation.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachment: trial_scope_template_v2.docx

From: Emma Carter <emma.carter@auralishealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: security@auralishealth.com
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Auralis trial: acceptance criteria, timeline, and eval methodology

Thanks Connor — appreciate the clear summary. We're aligned on the general approach; a few notes and tweaks from our side: 

Acceptance criteria tweaks (Auralis input):
- Quality: prefer a 4.2/5 threshold for discharge summaries (they're most sensitive) and 4.0/5 for others.
- Hallucination: agree with <= 2% but would like to capture severity buckets (minor vs. clinically material).
- Latency: 300ms P95 is acceptable, but we would request a soft target of 250ms for user-facing flows.

Timeline preference: we'd like to compress to 2 calendar weeks if possible (week 1 onboarding + offline evals; week 2 shadow run + fast review). We have a product review meeting on 3/23 where we want a preliminary readout.

Data & security: we'll provide a de-identified sample of 250 notes by EOD Monday (3/9). Security has started our questionnaire; they will request a limited SOC2 evidence package. I'll introduce you to our security lead in the next email.

Metrics we care about for the shadow run: per-example rubric score, hallucination flag (binary + severity), model confidence score, inference latency (p50/p95), and a short taxonomy of error type.

One ask: can Redwood provide a lightweight eval rubric (CSV template) we can use for the human grading side? Also confirm whether your shadow logging will include raw model outputs and whether those will be stored in our workspace or Redwood's secure bucket.

I'll re:confirm timeline after security sync. Looking forward — Emma

—
Emma Carter
Product Lead, Auralis Health
emma.carter@auralishealth.com

> Hi Emma / team — thanks again for the productive demo earlier. Quick recap and a proposed plan so we have aligned expectations before we hand off to ops/engineering...

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: connor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Auralis trial: acceptance criteria, timeline, and eval methodology

Connor — thanks for the thread. Quick internal notes on resourcing and what we should surface to Auralis: 

1) Resource plan: Marissa, can you own the offline rubric and grading coordination? We'll need someone from our infra team (SRE) allocated for the shadow logging hook and metric export (approx 0.5 FTE for the week).

2) Eval rubric (internal outline):
- Columns: example_id, note_type, rubric_score (1–5), hallucination_flag, hallucination_severity (none/minor/major), error_category, annotator, comments.
- Aggregates: mean rubric score by note_type, hallucination rate overall and by severity, latency percentiles.

3) Data handling: prefer Redwood to store shadow outputs in a dedicated customer bucket for compliance; provide short-lived access tokens to Auralis reviewers. Note: security asked that we not persist raw PHI anywhere; ensure de-identification steps are documented in the onboarding doc.

4) Timeline constraint: if Auralis wants a two-week compressed window, ops will need the data sample and security thumbprint no later than Monday EOD (3/9) to instrument by week start.

Marissa — can you prep the rubric template and a short ops checklist (what we need from Auralis, who to ping internally) by EOD today? I'll draft the SRE ask and cost estimate.

—
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Auralis trial: acceptance criteria, timeline, and eval methodology — kickoff and next steps

Emma / team — great, thanks for the fast turnaround and for starting security. Outline below is the updated compact plan and deliverables for kickoff.

Compact plan (2-week window):
- Day 0 (today): sign trial scope, we create work folder and share eval rubric template.
- Day 1–3: Auralis uploads 250 de-identified notes (per your note). Redwood runs offline evals against rubric and returns per-example results and aggregate dashboards.
- Day 4–9: Shadow run instrumentation + 5 business days of shadow traffic capture (read-only). We collect latency and model outputs and flag samples for human review.
- Day 10–11: Human grading of sampled shadow outputs (Auralis + Redwood reviewers).
- Day 12–13: Joint review meeting and verdict.

Deliverables we will provide at kickoff:
- eval_rubric_v1.md (attached) — CSV template and scoring guidance.
- auralis_data_instructions.txt — exact upload format and de-id checklist.
- secure Drive link with a shared bucket for artifacts (see shared Drive link above).

Security note: we'll store shadow outputs in a dedicated, encrypted Redwood bucket with short-lived access for Auralis reviewers. We'll not persist raw PHI — only de-identified outputs per our data handling checklist. Ops will provide the short-lived tokens during onboarding.

Next actions:
- Emma: confirm you received the attached rubric and the data instructions; upload the 250 notes by EOD Monday 3/9 if we're keeping the compressed timeline.
- Laura: assign the SRE contact and cost estimate — you mentioned a half-FTE; please confirm so we can include on the kickoff invite.
- Marissa: please upload the rubric template to the Drive link and create the grading doc for Auralis reviewers.

I'll schedule a 30-min kickoff for Wed 3/10 10:00am PT (tentative) — will send a calendar invite once we have confirmation.

Thanks all — excited to get this moving.

—
Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.com
